clue.text: Extremely small profit margin on an open razor

definitions.text: Extremely small profit margin on an open razor

parts.words: Extremely small profit margin on an open razor
parts.note: a rock-bottom selling price that leaves almost no margin, read also as the cost of an old-fashioned folding barber's blade

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper explains how little profit is made on selling a barber's open blade.
explanation.walkthrough: An open razor is called a cut-throat razor, so its price is literally a cut-throat price; the phrase also means a price slashed so low the seller barely profits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruinously low, competitive selling figure leaves the seller a tiny margin, the cut being as savage as a blade.

clue.text: Mild and bitter opponent of Henry VIII's second marriage plans

definitions.meaning: gentle, said of weather or of a merciful temper

definitions.text: bitter opponent of Henry VIII's second marriage plans
definitions.meaning: Pope ... VII, who refused to annul Henry's first marriage so he could wed Anne Boleyn

explanation.surface: A beer order of mild and bitter turns into a history of Tudor wedding politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mild and bitter' looks like a pub order of two beers; 'Mild' is one definition and 'bitter' belongs to the second, describing the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful or temperate, and Pope Clement VII blocked the annulment Henry sought before marrying Anne Boleyn.

clue.text: The last thing a French audience will stand for

definitions.text: The last thing a French audience will stand for

parts.words: The last thing a French audience will stand for
parts.note: reads as something French people would never tolerate, but means the piece they rise to their feet for at the end of a show

explanation.surface: Something so objectionable that French theatregoers would never tolerate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for' means tolerate in the surface, but literally the audience stands up: France's national anthem was traditionally played at the end of performances.
explanation.definitionFit: France's national anthem is played as an event closes and the crowd rises respectfully to hear it.

clue.text: At last he starts to warm up

indicators.note: starts says this word comes at the beginning, while 'last' sends the other word to the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finally begins to get warmer after being cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'At last' as 'AT comes last' and 'he starts' as 'HE comes first'.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat something is to raise its temperature, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Get a nib to become flexible

indicators.note: letters that become flexible can bend into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on softening a stiff pen point so it bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become flexible' rearranges ANIBTO; the first 'to' is a link joining the definition to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: He has about 8 different instructors

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the pronoun, so about signals a container
different asks for the letters to be made different, a rearrangement

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, a verb meaning responds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has around eight different teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 8 is a cross-reference to the answer at 8 down; 'different' rearranges that answer to TEACRS, and 'about' wraps it round the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers are people who instruct pupils, a synonym.

clue.text: House of Commons man in a rush, but not forgotten?

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the plant word

parts.note: a rush is a reed, a marsh plant
an MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP hurrying about yet still recalled by voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a rush' looks like haste, but rush is the plant REED, which is opened to hold MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remembered is kept in mind, the opposite of being forgotten.

clue.text: Caesar defied the senate to do it

definitions.text: Caesar defied the senate to do it

parts.words: Caesar defied the senate to do it
parts.note: Julius Caesar led his army over a small Italian river in 49 BC against the senate's orders, now a phrase for passing a point of no return

explanation.surface: A history note about Julius Caesar's defiance of Rome's senate.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking an army across the river out of his province was an act of war; the phrase now means making an irreversible commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's march over that river into Italy defied Rome and began civil war.

clue.text: Is responsive to stimulation about religious work

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Acts of the Apostles is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A churchgoer feels moved by a piece of sacred writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' tempts one to take RE (religious education), but ACTS, the New Testament book, is the religious work and 'about' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that reacts responds when stimulated, a synonym.

clue.text: A gentle review of refined style

indicators.note: a review looks over the letters again and rearranges them

explanation.surface: A mild critic writes a notice about a polished performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' signals a rearrangement of AGENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes something graceful and stylishly refined.

clue.text: Opening in a jacket that puts the Marines in a difficult situation

indicators.note: in says the Marines are put inside the predicament

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in trouble
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A tear in a jacket lands some soldiers in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts ... in' is the container signal; 'in a jacket' is part of the definition, not a second insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An armhole is the gap in a garment through which the arm passes.

clue.text: Back we come with an Irish boy, maybe

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people return home with a young lad from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the pronoun round to give EW; 'come with' just joins. 'maybe' shows the definition is by example: Ewan is one Irish or Scottish name among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewan is a boy's name used in Ireland and Scotland, given as one example.

clue.text: Lively tunes easy to pick up?

definitions.meaning: notes that weigh little, so easy to lift

explanation.surface: Catchy songs that anyone can learn quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' means learn in the surface, but the second reading is literal: music that is not heavy is easy to lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneful popular orchestral pieces are called light, and anything light is easy to lift.

clue.text: Where one might get a pail outside the Stock Exchange?

definitions.text: Where one might get a pail outside the Stock Exchange?

parts.words: Where one might get a pail outside the Stock Exchange?
parts.note: reads as a store for buckets but means an unofficial dealer in shares operating beyond the official market

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where to buy a bucket near the City's trading floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A bucket shop is an unregulated broker trading outside the official exchange; the surface reads it as a shop selling pails.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlicensed brokers taking bets on share prices away from the official market were nicknamed after pail stores.

clue.text: An even chance the matador won't want to take

definitions.meaning: a fifty-fifty matter, decided as if by a coin flip

definitions.text: the matador won't want to take
definitions.meaning: being hurled into the air on a bull's horns

explanation.surface: A bullfighter avoids a risky gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer literally: a matador does not want to be thrown up by the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip gives equal odds, and being flung skyward is the bullfighter's danger.

clue.text: Trees about right for rifle stocks

indicators.note: about says the tree word goes round the letter

parts.note: beeches are a kind of tree

explanation.surface: Timber from forests is used for gunstocks.
explanation.walkthrough: BEECHES round R; beech is indeed a wood used for gunstocks, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the rear part of a gun barrel joined to the stock, hence the plural for gun parts.

clue.text: One of the Beatles sporting his tweed jacket?

parts.note: Harris tweed is a cloth from the Outer Hebrides, made into jackets
if you are sporting a garment you have it on

explanation.surface: A member of a famous band wears his woollen coat.
explanation.walkthrough: George Harrison was the Beatles' lead guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison played guitar in the Liverpool band.

clue.text: Not so quick to understand about a painfully enlarged side feature?

indicators.note: about says the comparative goes round the single letter

parts.note: thicker means more stupid

explanation.surface: Someone slow on the uptake has a swollen face.
explanation.walkthrough: A thick ear is a swollen ear from a blow, so it is a feature on the side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip round the head leaves a swollen lug, a feature on the side of the head.

clue.text: Uses one's loaf in dealing with ink stains

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Working out how to remove ink marks takes brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses one's loaf' is British slang: loaf, from rhyming slang loaf of bread for head, means brain.
explanation.definitionFit: To use one's head is to reason or ponder.

clue.text: Search the bed again? How infuriating!

definitions.meaning: drag the river bed once more for a lost object
the cloth said to enrage a bull

explanation.surface: Being asked to look under the mattress twice is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: To drag a river is to search its bed with hooks; 'red rag to a bull' is something sure to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragging a river again is redragging, and a scarlet cloth provokes a bull.

clue.text: Not a child getting two points in a set

indicators.note: in places the compass points inside the collection

parts.note: a set is a group
W and N are compass points, west and north

explanation.surface: An adult gets a couple of points in a tennis set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' looks like scoring in tennis, but they are compass points W and N inside GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, someone no longer a minor.

clue.text: Countries which tastes vary

explanation.surface: Different nations have different palates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vary' rearranges TASTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A state is a nation or country.

clue.text: I'll repeat what has been said for those unable to read

definitions.note: the definition is a plural noun phrase; the answer serves as a collective noun, as in 'the illiterate'

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to iterate is to say again

explanation.surface: A teacher offers to say things again for pupils who can't read.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL plus ITERATE, joined by 'what has been said' being part of the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: People with no reading skills form a group called the unlettered.

clue.text: The Spanish currency held by the Bront

indicators.note: held by says the answer is enclosed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Old Spanish money owned by the literary sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: A currency is literally something that flows, so a river; the Ebro is a Spanish river, run of letters in 'thE BROnte(s)'.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a flow, so a river is a currency, and the Ebro flows through Spain.

clue.text: Jacob's first mate

parts.note: in Genesis Jacob's first wife, though he had wanted her sister Rachel; mate reads as a ship's officer

explanation.surface: The chief officer of a ship captained by Jacob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' sounds nautical, but it means the first wife of the biblical Jacob, married by Laban's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Laban's elder daughter was Jacob's first wife.

clue.text: They can't go straight on board

definitions.text: They can't go straight on board

parts.words: They can't go straight on board
parts.note: chess pieces that move in an L shape, read as people unable to reform aboard

explanation.surface: Criminals who can't reform once on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On a chessboard these pieces move two squares one way and one at right angles, never in a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces shaped like horses move in an L-shape, never straight.

clue.text: The Algerian city 1 down devastated

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 1 down, meaning mild

explanation.surface: A city in Algeria laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' is CLEMENT; 'devastated' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tlemcen is a historic city in north-western Algeria.

clue.text: What one must do to avoid drooping mentally!

definitions.text: What one must do to avoid drooping mentally!

parts.words: What one must do to avoid drooping mentally!
parts.note: advice to stay cheerful, read literally as holding the head high

explanation.surface: Advice on staying cheerful rather than sagging in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Drooping mentally means becoming low-spirited; the idiom for staying cheerful pictures a raised face.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means staying cheerful in adversity, pictured as a raised jaw.
